subject: POC kickoff - BrightLeaf / Redwood (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - BrightLeaf / Redwood (post-call recap)

Hi Mike,

Thanks for taking the time earlier today to walk us through BrightLeaf's search relevance use case. Quick recap of what I heard and recommended next steps for the POC.

Pain points:
- Search relevance drops for long-tail queries (product attributes & SKU combos).
- High latency and cost from current self-hosted reranking service during peak hours.
- Difficulty reproducing customer queries in staging for evals.

Goals:
1) Improve search precision (top-5 CTR) by >= 12% for targeted categories.
2) Reduce average rerank latency under 120ms P95.
3) Demonstrate stable costs at target throughput for 30 days.

Proposed POC scope (what we'll deliver):
- Dataset: 1M query+click pairs (sample of production), plus 5 category-specific prompt sets (~200 prompts each) for evaluation.
- Models: Redwood-optimized open reranker + a smaller latency-focused variant for fallback.
- Metrics: top-5 CTR lift, MRR, P95 latency, tokens-per-query cost estimate.
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week setup, 3-week evaluation, 1-week wrap-up).

Owners & roles:
- BrightLeaf: Mike Chen (product), Sarah Patel (data engineering).
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, engagement lead), Aditya Rao (SE, infra & access), Rishi Malhotra (solutions, success & SLOs).

Access & setup steps (BrightLeaf action items):
1) Share S3 sample path and a short schema description (fields: user_id, query, clicked_sku_id, timestamp).
2) Provide read-only IAM role or temporary signed credentials for ingestion (Aditya can advise on least-priv permissions).
3) Confirm list of 3 category SKUs to prioritize for prompt/eval creation.

Deliverables:
- POC runbook (attached draft): includes data ingestion steps, eval scripts, dashboards, and success criteria.
- Weekly status updates and a final presentation with recommendations.

Next steps:
- Mike: confirm access method and sample dataset by EOD 2027-02-23.
- Redwood: draft SOW & pricing estimate (Rishi) and schedule a 30-min kickoff (Aditya) for next week.

I've attached the POC runbook draft and an initial eval prompt template. Happy to adjust scope if you'd like a shorter proof or different success metrics.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments:
- redwood_poc_runbook_v0.3.pdf
- eval_prompt_templates.md

From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@brightleaf.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - BrightLeaf / Redwood (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Security: our infra team prefers VPC peering or PrivateLink for any model inference that touches PII; we can provide a private endpoint if needed.
2) Data: the sample S3 path will be available by 2027-02-22 but we need to scrub user identifiers; we can provide pseudonymized ids and a mapping table under controlled access.
3) Timeline: 6 weeks sounds good but can we push the evaluation window to 4 weeks (2-week setup, 4-week eval) given our internal QA cycle?

We'll confirm the exact S3 path and the IAM approach by EOD Monday (2027-02-22). Sarah will be your point for data access.

Also, budget: we have an internal cap for a pilot at ~$35k. If the SOW comes in higher, we'll need to route for an exec sign-off.

Happy to jump on a short kickoff next week — how's Wednesday 2027-02-24 10am PT for your team?

Best,
Mike
Product Manager, BrightLeaf
